rules.rule: Complete required rezoning, concept, preliminary, final plan, and plat approvals before the dependent construction permit; approved plans and conditions remain controlling.

Apply Overland Park's adopted building, residential, existing-building, plumbing, mechanical, fuel-gas, fire, electrical, energy, and pool codes together with local amendments and applicable accessibility requirements.
Required architectural and engineering documents must be signed and sealed by the appropriate Kansas-licensed design professional.
Verify the applicable Johnson County contractor license, responsible trade classification, insurance, and bond before permit issuance; a license does not authorize work outside its classification.
A building permit expires after 180 days without a qualifying inspection; an approved inspection extends it for another 180 days.
Do not occupy until building, fire, planning, engineering, utility, accessibility, and other required finals are approved or formally deferred under an authorized temporary occupancy.

Engineering permit issuance requires applicable contractor credentials, insurance and bonding, approved plans, and fees; work must follow current City construction criteria and inspection requirements.
Obtain approval before constructing, erecting, altering, relocating, or displaying a regulated sign; comply with UDO Chapter 18.440 and any approved sign plan or event condition.
An Overland Park permit does not replace separate Johnson County, Kansas state, KDOT, KDHE, or federal authorization triggered by the site or operation.
Before opening, verify the exact operation has a valid certificate of occupancy and every operation-specific City, county, state, fire, health, alcohol, rental, alarm, or event approval that applies.
One operational approval does not replace another required specialty, state, fire, health, alcohol, rental, alarm, event, or zoning approval; resolve every triggered workflow separately.
Verify the approval is issued for the correct operator, activity, and address and remains unexpired; complete every required renewal, inspection, insurance, credential, and reporting obligation.

Temporary occupancy is prohibited until the applicable final inspection authorizes consideration, the City approves and signs the certificate, and the applicant signs and returns it; complete deficiencies or obtain an extension before expiration.

Submit the exact event category application and every dependent closure, alcohol, food, fire, structure, and signage request by the deadline stated in the official event instructions; an event application does not authorize activity before approval.

Verify land-use compatibility, traffic and emergency access, parking rights, sanitation, waste, hours, frequency, noise, temporary structures, signs, food and alcohol service, fire safety, insurance, and site restoration against the selected event category and approval conditions.

Identify the adopted code editions, local amendments, project scope, occupancy and use, construction type, building area and height, mixed-use method, allowable increases, and existing-building compliance path; reconcile the analysis with the plans.

Verify occupant loads, means-of-egress capacity and arrangement, travel distance, common path, dead ends, exits, doors, stairs, guards, emergency lighting, exit signs, fire-resistance ratings, opening protection, shafts, and fire-protection features applicable to the work.

Verify accessible route, site arrival, parking, entrances, doors, circulation, toilet and bathing rooms, service counters, dwelling or sleeping units, signage, reach ranges, alarms, and alteration obligations under the adopted code and applicable federal standards.

Verify design criteria, loads and combinations, soils and foundation basis, lateral system, member design, connections, special inspections, deferred structural items, and structural continuity across architectural and engineering documents.

Verify the applicable energy compliance path, envelope assemblies and fenestration, air sealing, lighting and controls, mechanical efficiency and controls, service-water heating, commissioning, and required testing agree with the construction documents.

Reconcile equipment, loads, demand, service sizes, distribution, clearances, ventilation, combustion air, exhaust, plumbing fixtures, water and sewer, gas, controls, penetrations, firestopping, access, listings, and shutdown interfaces across all disciplines.

Complete every inspection and test applicable to the approved scope, upload required correction and special-inspection records, resolve permit conditions, and obtain final approval before occupancy or use; an unapproved inspection is not closeout.

Verify the address-derived base district, subzone, parcel ordinance, approved plan, permitted/special/accessory use classification, and every applicable supplemental-use condition against the current UDC and official records.

Calculate and compare lot and district area, lot width, density, height, setbacks/build-to lines, open space, parking, loading, landscaping, lighting, signs, access, and other fixed or approved-plan development standards; missing controlling plan values remain not verified.

Verify applicable architectural, site, streetscape, pedestrian, compatibility, screening, outdoor-storage, performance, and area-specific design standards, including City Center guidelines and approved development-agreement conditions where applicable.
Verify adequate water and fire flow, wastewater, stormwater, roads and access, utilities, and other public services before plan or plat approval, together with required dedications and improvements.

Legal description, ownership, boundaries, uses, dimensions, grading, utilities, drainage, access, architecture, landscaping, lighting, signs, phasing, deviations, and conditions must agree across concept, preliminary, final, plat, civil, and building records.

Complete required neighborhood or public notice, staff, Planning Commission, City Council, recording, and condition-resolution steps in the prescribed sequence; an application or recommendation is not final approval.

Verify the civil design follows current Overland Park criteria, specifications, standard details, approved final plan, survey control, utility coordination, easements, responsible professional seals, and project-specific approval conditions.

Reconcile existing and proposed drainage areas, design storms, runoff, storm-system capacity, detention or treatment, overflow routes, erosion controls, receiving waters, flood hazards, and maintenance across reports and plans.

Verify work limits, ownership and easements, traffic and pedestrian control, access, utility locates, trench and pavement restoration, ADA facilities, bonds, insurance, inspections, as-builts, and acceptance for all public or right-of-way work.

Calculate total and common-plan disturbance; implement approved erosion and sediment controls before disturbance, perform required inspections and corrections, protect adjacent property and right-of-way, and maintain coverage through final stabilization.

Verify service provider, available water/wastewater capacity, connection point, service size, demand and discharge, backflow or pretreatment, private-system eligibility, fees, inspections, and activation conditions from authoritative provider records.

Service routes, sizes, elevations, fixtures, equipment, separations, capacities, approvals, and connection details must agree across provider applications, civil plans, plumbing plans, site plans, and building records.

Identify occupancy, hazards, fire-flow and water-supply basis, required alarm/suppression/standpipe/hood or hazardous-material systems, adopted standards, design criteria, impairments, and interfaces with the building life-safety strategy.

Verify system layout, coverage, device or nozzle selection, hydraulic and electrical calculations, water supply, supervision, sequence of operations, emergency power, controls, monitoring, fire department access and connections, listings, and cross-discipline coordination.

Complete required rough and final inspections, flushing, pressure, alarm, integrated, functional, acceptance, and contractor certification records; resolve deficiencies before system activation, occupancy, or operation.

Verify the exact operation is allowed by zoning, matches the certificate of occupancy and approved floor area, and has every required general, specialty, state, health, fire, alcohol, rental, alarm, or event approval before opening.

Verify ownership, operator and manager qualifications, location, hours, capacity, equipment, safety systems, insurance, inspections, employee or contractor credentials, records, and all operation-specific license conditions.
Track expiration and renewal, continuing inspections and reporting, and required notice or new approval for ownership, name, address, space, process, equipment, capacity, or other material changes.

Resolve state or federal jurisdiction from authoritative route, environmental, facility, emission, disturbance, asbestos, and aquatic-resource facts; absence of a local permit trigger does not establish that outside approval is unnecessary.

Obtain the applicable state or federal authorization before regulated disturbance, demolition, construction, discharge, or right-of-way work and comply with every condition, inspection, monitoring, reporting, mitigation, and closeout requirement.
